name.en-US: The Twelve Degrees of Humility and Pride
name.pt-BR: Os doze graus da humildade e do orgulho

description.en-US: Barton R. V. Mills's English (SPCK, 1929) of Bernard's first treatise, in twenty-two chapters under two parts: the twelve degrees of humility (chapters I-IX) and the twelve degrees of pride (X-XXII). Mills's chapters differ from the Latin book's, so this is a separate book of the same work.
description.pt-BR: A tradução inglesa de Barton R. V. Mills (1929) do tratado de São Bernardo sobre os graus da humildade e do orgulho.

sources.edition: The Twelve Degrees of Humility and Pride, by Saint Bernard, translated by Barton R. V. Mills (London: SPCK, 1929), Translations of Christian Literature, Series II, Latin Texts.
sources.description: Djvu OCR cleaned by script, not proofread. Mills's preface and long introduction are not imported; his footnotes are kept as footnotes where the OCR keeps the markers legible and dropped otherwise.
sources.tierEvidence: Published in 1929, before 1931: public domain in the US.

title.en-US: Part I. The Twelve Degrees of Humility
Chapter I. The search for Truth — Christ the goal and the road

Chapter II. The ladder of humility, foreshadowed by that which Jacob saw in his vision. The refreshment provided by Christ — humility, love, and contemplation — of which love is the central course, as on Solomon's table

Chapter III. The process by which the road of humility leads to the attainment of Truth. The three degrees of Truth. The teaching of Christ about these. Discussion of the difficulty involved in the statement that He learned compassion through suffering
Chapter IV. The first degree of Truth — self-scrutiny — reveals to us our own evil case
Chapter V. The second degree of Truth — -wherein consciousness of our own shortcomings makes us merciful to those of other people
Chapter VI. The third, degree of Truth — the clearing of the spiritual sight, so that it may gaze on holy and heavenly things
Chapter VII. The -work of the Persons of the Holy Trinity in leading men through the three degrees of Truth
Chapter VIII. The same sequence is seen in the 'rapture' of St. Paul to the third heaven
Chapter IX. The writer sighs regretfully over his own shortcomings in the search for Truth
